documents.summary: A 2023 provost working-group report that sets no university-wide AI rule. It leaves require-or-prohibit decisions to instructors, asks that choices be stated in the syllabus, sets integrity and attestation rules, and offers sample syllabus statements at prohibit, allow-with-attribution and encourage levels. It also gives recommendations on research, tool vetting, legal issues and training.
documents.stance_why: The report says 'UAB does not dictate that teachers shall require or prohibit the use of generative AI' and hands course decisions to teachers, offering sample prohibit, attribution and encourage statements, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

notes: Reconciled from two independent codings (v2/run/coderA and coderB). The UAB 'Generative AI and UAB Policy' page was inaccessible (404) and is not coded. The provost report's clinical and medical sections were skipped as not about teaching or learning. The CTL page repeats the report's sample syllabus statements (without the computer-code allow-with-attribution sample); each document was coded on its own. Neither coder coded the report's sentence 'Clear and concise course policies and explicit instructions ...' (it appears in the CTL page and is coded there). Recurring UNCOVERED notes: risk statements about AI-enabled cheating and plagiarism, human-contact and feedback concerns, and dissemination of the guidance; none yet mapped to an existing type. Course layer is deferred and no school or computing policy was found.
